messages:
June: Quick question — we have a contractor starting 11/10 who may accrue a few sick days. If they end up with unused sick time at offboarding, can we convert it to a floating holiday or a one-time PTO payout? Need a clear answer for the offer package.

Olivia (People Ops): Short answer: usually no automatic conversion for sick -> PTO. Sick is separate. But we do have two exceptions (see below) and a manual approval path. @Lina can confirm payroll constraints. :thinking_face:

Sam (Eng): Is this different for contractors vs W-2s? The offer language needs to be exact.

Olivia (People Ops): Yes — contractors are handled case-by-case depending on the contract. For W-2 employees, accrued sick follows state regs (no convert/payout in many states). For contractors, we may be able to do a one-time top-up if the manager covers cost and Legal signs off. It's not standard.

Mike (Manager): If it helps, the budget for this hire is flexible. We're ok covering a small top-up if that smooths the offer. What's the approval flow?

Lina (Payroll): Payroll note: we can do a one-time discretionary payout but it must be processed before the final invoice period closes. Need: written approval from manager + People Ops signoff + invoice flag. Cutoff for Nov payroll is 11/28.

Olivia (People Ops): Policy excerpt: `Sick leave accruals are governed by contract and local law. Sick balances are generally not eligible for conversion to PTO or cash unless expressly approved by People Ops & Finance. To request: submit a manual exception ticket (people-ops), attach manager approval, and cc payroll.`

June: Perfect — I'll add the manual exception clause in the offer and loop in Mike/Lina. Also one more related ask: our team has a product launch on 12/18 and one of the ICs is asking for a blackout exception to take 3 days off right before the launch. What's the quickest path for that?

Mike (Manager): Short answer: we typically deny blackout time in the 2-week window unless we can fully cover duties. But if the IC is remote and can be on-call for the 18th, we might approve. Need coverage plan + backup.

Olivia (People Ops): For operational blackout requests: manager must submit the coverage plan in the exception ticket. Include who will cover, overlap days, and confirmation they can be on-call. People Ops will triage for fairness. If it's mission-critical launch coverage, we can offer a compensatory floating day after launch.

Sam (Eng): To confirm — compensatory floating day = 1 extra PTO day added to balance after launch? Is that tracked automatically or manual?

Lina (Payroll): Manual process. People Ops tells Payroll the grant ID and we apply 1 discretionary day to that employee's balance within 2 pay cycles.

June: Awesome, thanks. I'll draft the offer language: mention "manual exception possible; subject to People Ops/Payroll signoff and manager approval" and include blackout pro tip for launch coverage.

people-ops-bot: New exception ticket created: #HR-2026-342 — please attach manager approval and coverage plan. ETA triage 2 business days.

Olivia (People Ops): Thanks all. June — once you have manager approval, drop the doc in the ticket and ping me. I'll route to Legal if this becomes a contractor pay amendment. :white_check_mark:
